channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Russia's LDPR proposes 5% tax on migrant money transfers abroad
item.description: Russia's Liberal Democratic Party (LDPR) has proposed a mandatory 5% tax on money transfers sent abroad by foreign citizens. Banks and payment systems would automatically deduct the fee, sending it to the federal budget. The party claims this would boost the Russian economy and help cover costs associated with foreign citizens in Russia. Experts estimate migrants send around $25 billion out of Russia annually.

item.title: Uzbek President addresses first Central Asia-South Korea summit in Seoul
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev expressed admiration for Seoul's development during his visit for the first Central Asia-South Korea summit. He thanked South Korean President Lee Jae-myung for the summit's organization, highlighting the long-standing, mutually respectful relationship between the nations, rooted in the Great Silk Road. He affirmed Uzbekistan's support for peace on the Korean Peninsula.

item.title: Uzbekistan Approves New Privatization List for State Assets
item.description: Uzbekistan has approved a new list of large state assets to be privatized, following a presidential decree to reduce state participation in the economy. The sale includes stakes in financial institutions, industrial, transport, and trade enterprises. Conditions for selling state assets and land plots are also being updated.

item.title: Uzbek President Proposes Five Strategic Cooperation Areas with South Korea
item.description: At the first Central Asia-Republic of Korea summit in Seoul, Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev proposed cooperation in five strategic areas: security, mutually beneficial practical collaboration, and expanding humanitarian exchanges. He acknowledged South Korea's early recognition of Central Asia's potential and its contribution to industrialization and infrastructure development.

item.title: Kazakhstan proposes new method for calculating damage from tree felling
item.description: Kazakhstan is considering a new approach to calculating damages for illegal tree and shrub destruction. A parliament member suggests factoring in the tree's species, conservation status, recovery potential, and ecological significance, rather than just quantity.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes Uniting Central Asia and South Korea's Potential
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev proposed uniting the potential of Central Asia and South Korea at the first "Central Asia - Republic of Korea" business summit. He highlighted the region's 80 million population, growing demand, and vast resources. Uzbekistan's mineral resources are valued at $3 trillion, with 120 projects planned.

item.title: Uzbekistan State Budget Revenues Increase by 44% in Six Months
item.description: Uzbekistan's state budget revenues grew by nearly 44% in the first six months of the year. According to the Minister of Economy and Finance, Jamshid Kuchkarov, 72% of budget revenues came from taxes and 20% from duties. The largest portion of expenditures was allocated to the education sector.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to introduce eight new online notary services by October 1
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Justice will launch eight new online notary services on October 1, expanding remote access via the Electronic Notary app. This digitalization effort aims to improve service accessibility, reduce office queues, and promote paperless document management. By December 1, four more services will be added, bringing the total to 21, allowing one-third of notarial actions to be done online.

item.title: Osh police search markets and car washes for children not attending school
item.description: Police in Osh, Kyrgyzstan, are conducting raids on markets, car washes, and other public places to identify minors who are not attending school, are unsupervised, or are in difficult life situations. The operation, part of the 'Salam, Mektep!' campaign, aims to ensure children's safety, their right to education, and prevent juvenile delinquency.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to introduce eight new online notary services by October 1
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Justice will launch eight new online notary services on October 1, expanding remote access via the Electronic Notary app. This digitalization effort aims to improve service accessibility, reduce office queues, and promote paperless document management. By December 1, four more services will be added, bringing the total to 21, allowing one-third of notarial actions to be done online.

item.title: Uzbekistan Adopts AI Strategy to Enhance Governance and Public Services
item.description: Uzbekistan has approved a strategy for artificial intelligence development until 2030, aiming to integrate AI in healthcare, education, agriculture, finance, and public services. The goal is to reduce bureaucracy, improve management quality, and increase accessibility of state services.

item.title: Zelensky Claims Russian Drones Entered Moldova Twice While His Plane Was Present
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Russian drones entered Moldova's airspace twice while his presidential plane was in the country. He believes Russia may have targeted his plane and used similar tactics in other European countries.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to implement supervisory technologies in banking sector by 2026
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's National Bank approved a concept and roadmap for supervisory technologies (SupTech) development from 2026-2031. The program aims to automate regulatory processes using AI, machine learning, and big data, aligning with global digital standards and enhancing cyber resilience in the banking sector.

item.title: Bishkek and Seoul Establish Sister City Relations
item.description: The mayors of Bishkek and Seoul signed a memorandum establishing sister city relations between the two capitals. The agreement, signed in Seoul during President Japarov's visit, aims to foster cooperation in trade, economy, culture, education, and urban management.

item.title: Bishkek activist urges mayor to use public transport to improve city life
item.description: An activist has urged the mayor of Bishkek to lead by example by using public transport to demonstrate how to make the city comfortable for all residents. She linked transport and environmental issues to decision-making processes and advocated for an elected mayor and greater citizen participation in urban policy.

item.title: Uzbek MP Alisher Qodirov objects to preserving Tashkent cultural heritage site
item.description: Uzbek MP Alisher Qodirov has objected to the preservation of a cultural heritage site in Tashkent, stating the Agency for Cultural Heritage should prioritize national culture. The agency confirmed the building is under state protection and has appealed to the Prosecutor General's Office to prevent its demolition.

item.title: Uzbek President invites South Korean companies to invest in artificial intelligence in Karakalpakstan
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has invited South Korean companies to invest in artificial intelligence projects in Karakalpakstan. He highlighted AI's potential to create at least $10 billion in added value for every country's economy within five years.

item.title: Dushanbe Hosts Conference on Strengthening State Cooperation with Overseas Diasporas
item.description: A national conference on engaging Tajik diasporas and compatriots abroad as development partners was held in Dushanbe. Organized by the Ministry of Labor, Migration and Employment, the event aimed to foster dialogue and leverage the potential of diasporas for sustainable national development.

item.title: Kyrgyz President invites Korean business to participate in major infrastructure projects
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov invited Korean companies to join the construction of the Kambarat-1 HPP, development of the 'Ala-Too Resort', and creation of logistics centers along the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway. He urged a shift from discussions to project implementation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan sees decline in private housing completions in first eight months of 2026
item.description: In January-August 2026, Kyrgyzstan commissioned 6,009 individual residential buildings, a 0.7 percent decrease compared to the previous year. Bishkek and Batken region saw growth, while Jalal-Abad, Osh, Chui, Talas, and Issyk-Kul regions experienced declines.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Considers Lifting Ban on New Airline Company Registrations
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering lifting the moratorium on registering and certifying new airlines. The State Civil Aviation Agency proposed the draft presidential decree, stating that the goals of the moratorium have been achieved and identified violations have been rectified.

item.title: Uzbekistan's economy grew 8.5% in first half of 2026, budget deficit at 0.7% of GDP
item.description: Uzbekistan's consolidated budget deficit was 0.7% of GDP in the first half of 2026. The economy grew 8.5%, driven by services, construction, industry, investment, and exports. Annual inflation stood at 6.4%.

item.title: Uzbekistan proposes 'cooperation for rapid development' vision with Central Asia and South Korea
item.description: Uzbekistan has proposed developing a long-term conceptual vision titled 'Central Asia - Republic of Korea: Cooperation for Rapid Development'. The initiative was put forward by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev at the first summit between the region's countries and South Korea in Seoul.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Customs Disrupt Synthetic Drug Smuggling Channel in Bishkek
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Northern Railway Customs and the Interior Ministry's anti-drug service have dismantled an illegal mephedrone smuggling operation in Bishkek. An 18-year-old woman was detained with a large quantity of the synthetic drug, which could have generated over 10 million soms.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Introduce Monthly Allowances for Medical Personnel Starting January 1
item.description: Starting January 1, certain medical professionals in Uzbekistan will receive monthly allowances based on their qualifications. Graduates of bachelor's programs will receive one minimum wage, master's graduates two, and family medicine specialists four.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Sees Decline in Private Housing Construction in August
item.description: In January-August, Kyrgyzstan commissioned 6,009 private homes totaling 822,900 square meters, with investments reaching 26.2 billion soms. However, housing area put into operation decreased by 0.7% compared to the previous year, reversing a positive trend.

item.title: Temporary Ban Imposed on Importing Certain Construction Materials to Kyrgyzstan
item.description: The Cabinet of Ministers has temporarily banned the import of certain construction materials into Kyrgyzstan for six months. The decision aims to protect domestic producers, stabilize the internal market, and ensure economic security against import competition.

item.title: Central Asia and Korea agree on biennial summits and expanded cooperation
item.description: Central Asian nations and Korea agreed to hold biennial summits, with the next in Astana in 2028. Cooperation will focus on air connectivity, trade, critical minerals processing, energy, and AI digitalization. Foreign ministers will monitor agreement implementation.

item.title: Vietnamese ROX Group Considers Major Investment Projects in Uzbekistan
item.description: Vietnam's ROX Group is exploring new investment projects in several regions of Uzbekistan, including Bukhara, Samarkand, and Jizzakh. In Bukhara, a project valued at $2 billion aims to construct modern real estate, residential areas, schools, and infrastructure on over 85 hectares, potentially creating 5,000-6,000 jobs and improving housing for over 50,000 citizens.

item.title: Gender Stereotypes Impacting Justice System in Uzbekistan, Expert Claims
item.description: An expert on gender issues and founder of the Nemolchi.uz anti-violence project in Uzbekistan, Irina Matvienko, criticizes a court ruling that blamed a victim of domestic violence for the crime. Matvienko argues such phrasing reflects gender stereotypes, leading to victim-blaming and potentially influencing how the state portrays violence.

item.title: New Monthly Allowances for Nurses and Family Doctors in Uzbekistan Effective 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan has established a system for paying monthly allowances to nurses and family doctors. Starting January 1, 2027, nurses and medical assistants who complete master's degrees will receive a monthly allowance equivalent to twice the minimum wage, while those with bachelor's degrees will receive one times the minimum wage.

item.title: Uzbek President Proposes Five Initiatives to Boost Central Asia-South Korea Cooperation
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev put forward five proposals to develop cooperation between Central Asia and South Korea. These initiatives focus on long-term partnership, trade and investment, critical minerals, green development, and human capital development. The proposals aim to strengthen regional ties and economic collaboration.

item.title: Uzbekistan Tightens Admission and Training Requirements for Medical and Pharmaceutical Fields
item.description: Uzbekistan has significantly tightened admission and training requirements for medical and pharmaceutical fields, according to a presidential decree. The new measures aim to fundamentally improve the system of training personnel in these sectors, introducing strict criteria for admissions, exam scores, and study procedures.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Central Bank Maintains Key Interest Rate at 14% Amid Inflationary Risks
item.description: The Central Bank of Uzbekistan has kept its key interest rate unchanged at 14% annually. Despite a downward trend in inflation and signs of economic rebalancing, the regulator cited persistent risks that could increase inflation, necessitating the continuation of current tight monetary conditions.

item.title: Uzbekistan Faces High Risk of Nitazenes, Synthetic Opioids, Despite No Detections Yet
item.description: Uzbekistan faces a high risk of nitazenes, synthetic opioids hundreds of times stronger than heroin, despite no confirmed cases. Customs seized nearly 1.9 tons of drugs in early 2024, but nitazenes were absent. The committee considers the risk high due to global drug market shifts, including China's control over fentanyl-like substances and Afghanistan's poppy cultivation ban.

item.title: Uzbekistan proposes gradual pension age increase starting 2028
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Economy and Finance proposed a gradual increase in the retirement age, starting in 2028. The plan aims to raise the age to 63 for men and 58 for women by 2039. Measures are included to protect pre-retirement workers and allow early pension access for the unemployed.

item.title: Hong Kong unveils first five-year socio-economic development plan
item.description: Hong Kong has presented its first five-year socio-economic development plan, aiming to consolidate and enhance its advantages in international finance, shipping, trade, innovation, and technology. The plan seeks to integrate the region more effectively into China's overall development and support the "one country, two systems" policy.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Central Bank keeps key interest rate at 14 percent
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank has maintained its key interest rate at 14 percent. The regulator cited the need to continue current tight monetary and credit conditions due to persistent inflationary risks. The decision aims to stabilize prices and support economic growth.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan updates migration rules for Tajik citizens
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has updated its migration regulations. The changes specify new procedures for citizens of Tajikistan. Information regarding the updated requirements for Tajik nationals is now available.

item.title: Tajikistan Delegation Attends 70th IAEA General Conference in Vienna
item.description: A delegation from Tajikistan is participating in the 70th General Conference of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) in Vienna, running from September 14-18. The delegation is led by Deputy Foreign Minister Nigina Alizoda and includes officials from the Ministry of Industry and New Technologies and the National Academy of Sciences. Discussions will focus on the safe and peaceful use of nuclear technologies.
